body: You can start a game three ways: from the game list in the left sidebar, from the game grid on the start screen, or straight from this wiki via the pre-game screen.
Before every game the pre-game screen appears: pick the mode there (e.g. single or multiplayer) and reach the options and this wiki.
- [Esc] pauses and resumes the running game - in menus it goes back.
- [F11] toggles fullscreen on and off.
- The green Back to menu button ends the game and saves the high score.
On the left you see all games with their icon and your high score (star). The running game stays highlighted; on small windows the list scrolls with the mouse wheel.
The status card at the bottom left shows the game name, state (green = running, gold = paused, red = game over), score and the current frame rate.
Snake, Pong, Air Hockey, Tic-Tac-Toe, Tetris (Versus) and Asteroids (co-op duel) have a local 2-player mode - selectable on the pre-game screen.
In single player both key bindings control the same character; in multiplayer one each (default: P1 = WASD, P2 = arrows or IJKL - see options).
Toggle sound and set the volume in the options screen. All effects are generated live - there are no audio files.
Haptics vibrates a connected gamepad (does nothing without one).
Three presets are available: WASD + arrows, WASD + IJKL and arrows + WASD.
Every single key can be rebound: click a row or confirm with Enter, then press the desired key. [Esc] cancels.
Bindings are separate for player 1 and player 2 and are saved permanently.
The resolution sets the internal play area (480x360 up to 1280x960). Smaller = less load, bigger = sharper image.
Auto-resolution adapts the play area to the window size automatically.
The FPS options (15 to 120) set the target frame rate - fewer FPS saves power.
The interface is available in German, English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. Switch in the options screen or via Language in the sidebar - this wiki switches language too.
Every game saves its best value automatically when a round ends. A new record shows a golden banner - plus confetti rain.
You can see the best values everywhere: as a star in the sidebar list, in the ticker on the start screen and in the status card.
- settings.json: sound, volume, key bindings, resolution, FPS and game options (e.g. Snake mode, Sudoku settings).
- mem.json: high scores, the chosen language and the Sudoku level progress.
- mem-ngb.json: Snake's visual mods (head color, grid, banner).
Both files live right in the game folder and can simply be deleted to reset.
Points are only saved when you leave via Back to menu or the round ends normally - not when the window is closed hard mid-game.

The collection now tracks your progress: 69 achievements and detailed statistics across all 38 games. Both live behind the Achievements & Stats button in the sidebar; switch between the two tabs with [Tab] or a click.
There are three categories:
- General: collection-wide goals such as games started, games tried, total play time, records broken and wins - plus little extras like the Night Owl (play after midnight).
- Score milestones: one fair target score per game, tuned to its scoring scale.
- Special moments: checkmating the AI, a YAHTZEE, the 2048 tile, a Wordle in 2 tries and more.
Unlocking shows a golden toast in the top-right corner with a little fanfare - even mid-game.
Existing data counts: on the first launch after the update, your old high scores are credited automatically (without the toast fireworks).
Locked achievements show a progress bar, unlocked ones their date.
Cards at the top sum everything up: total play time, games played, wins, records broken, games tried and your achievement count - plus your favourite game (most play time).
Below, a table lists every game you have played with plays, time, wins and best score, sorted by play time. Clicking a row jumps straight to that game.
Only active play time counts - pauses and menus don't. Wins are tracked by games with a clear win/lose outcome (board, card and puzzle games) in single-player.
Everything is stored locally in mem.json (sections stats and achievements), together with your language and high scores. Deleting the file also resets achievements and statistics.

Endless mode with level climbing: you start with exactly one apple. The more apples you collect in total, the higher your level - more apples appear at once and the score multiplier rises (15 levels, up to x16).
- Blue apples open a slot machine: the stake is your length, three equal symbols = jackpot with bonus apples.
- Purple apples (gambling) bet part of your size: normally a 50 percent stake with a factor of x0.5 to x1.5.
Your exact size is shown as a decimal in the top left - every bet builds on it. The level tiers live in games/levels/snake-comp.json and are freely editable.
Toggle with [H] in the competitive setup: every boost eats length, and purple apples get riskier (75 to 90 percent stake, factor x0.25 to x2.25). A red border marks the mode.
Reachable with [P] in single player: collected apples can be converted into prestige levels that grant lasting perks. Progress persists across runs.
In the setup via the brush button or [C] : a pure looks menu that never changes gameplay.
- Head: the snake's head color (presets or a custom RGB color).
- Grid: a coordinate grid with row numbers and column letters as a guide on big boards.
- Banner: toggle the multiplier banner, plus size and opacity - with live preview.
Everything is stored in mem-ngb.json.
With [V] in the setup: the board is rendered as a 3D scene, a chase camera floats behind the snake and steering is relative to the view direction (two quick presses = U-turn).
With [K] you open the 3D camera options: smooth shake, field of view (FOV), camera height and the turn-shake toggle. Playable in 3D: Classic and Obstacles (single player only).
Steer with [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrow keys. In 3D you steer relative to the view direction: left/right turn, two quick presses = U-turn.
- Boost: hold [Space] or Shift = double speed. The stamina bar drains and recharges afterwards.
- Player 2 boosts with Enter or the right Shift key.
- Classic: pure snake.
- Speed rush: every food makes you faster.
- Obstacles: deadly blocks on the board.
- Portals: teleporter pairs move you across the board.
- Time attack: 60 seconds, as many apples as possible.
- Competitive: endless mode with levels, slot machine and gamble apples - details on the Snake special page.
Also selectable: wall wrap, bonus apples, hardcore, 2D/3D view with [V] and multiplayer.
Apples give points (bonus apples randomly double). Gold apples appear temporarily, give lots of points and refill the boost instantly. In competitive your level multiplies all points.
- Use the boost on long straights, not in tight corners.
- With wrap enabled you can escape over the edge when you box yourself in.
- In competitive, purple apples pay off best when you have spare length to stake.
Player 1 moves the left paddle with [W] and [S] - in multiplayer, player 2 controls the right one with the arrow keys.
The movement mode is switchable per control: continuous (press once, paddle keeps going) or hold (moves only while pressed). Toggle with [X] for control 1 and [N] for control 2.
Play to 5 points, against the AI or with two players.
The ball physics accelerate with every hit; the bounce angle depends on where the ball meets the paddle.
- Hit the ball with the paddle edge to create steep angles.
- Hold mode gives finer control, continuous mode faster reactions.
In single player your mallet follows the mouse - any key switches back to keyboard control (8 directions).
In multiplayer P1 plays left with [W] [A] [S] [D] and P2 right with [I] [J] [K] [L] .
- AI difficulty: easy, medium or hard.
- [T] picks the goals to win (3/5/7/10).
- [P] toggles power-ups: XL (bigger mallet), GOAL (opponent's goal shrinks), speed (faster mallet). Power-ups belong to the player who touched the puck last.
- The puck inherits your mallet speed - build momentum instead of just blocking.
- Stay behind the puck: pushing it towards your own goal risks own goals.
Place marks with a mouse click. After the game ends: Enter or click = new round, [S] = back to the settings.
Board sizes from 3x3 up to 9x9. The winning length adapts: 3 in a row on 3x3, 4 on 4x4, otherwise 5.
Single player against the AI (easy/medium/hard) or two players locally, X versus O in turns.
- The hard AI on 3x3 is unbeatable - a draw is the best you can get there.
- On big boards the center matters most: most 5-lines pass through it.
Move the paddle with the mouse or arrow keys. [Space] launches the ball and fires the laser. [P] or [Esc] pauses.
- [1] [2] [3] picks the difficulty.
- Left/right changes the ball color, up/down the start level, [M] the layout (standard or full).
Brick types: normal, steel (indestructible), bomb (explodes) and gold (extra points).
Power-ups: x2/x3 balls, [L] laser, [F] fireball, [G] sticky, [U] shield, coins for bonus points - plus a combo multiplier for fast hits.
- Play the ball along the side walls behind the brick block - it clears by itself up there.
- The shield catches exactly one breakthrough: save it for risky multiball phases.
Left/right moves the piece, up rotates it, down is the soft drop and the action key (default: [Space] ) the hard drop.
Full rows score points - several at once score much more. Every 10 rows the level and speed increase.
Versus (multiplayer): two boards side by side, whoever's stack hits the top first loses.
- Keep one column free for the long I-piece and clear with quadruple rows.
- Build flat: tall towers tip over quickly as the speed rises.
- Classic: the classic alien block descends. In the setup you choose movement (left/right only or free with WASD) and aiming (always up or at the mouse).
- Arena: free movement in all directions, enemies stream in from all edges, you aim in your movement direction.
Four weapons, switch with [1] to [4] : blaster, spread shot, rapid fire and laser.
Destroyed aliens drop power-ups: extra life, shield and weapon upgrades. Every 4th level has a boss.
- The spread shot clears dense blocks, the laser pierces whole columns - switch per wave.
- Never stand still in the arena: circle along the edge and pull enemies into a line.
Up thrusts in the view direction, left/right rotates the ship, the action key fires. The ship keeps drifting (inertia) and wraps around the screen edges.
Down triggers hyperspace: an emergency jump to a random position with a 4 second cooldown - and a 12 percent risk of breaking apart.
Rocks split into two smaller ones; the three sizes give 20/50/100 points. The UFO (can be disabled) gives 200 points, an extra life comes every 5000 points.
Power-ups from destroyed rocks: shield (6 seconds invulnerable), triple shot and rapid fire.
Co-op duel (multiplayer): both ships fly at once with separate lives - whoever has more points wins.
- Clear the small, fast splinters first before you crack the next big rock.
- Hyperspace is a last resort, not a travel option - the risk is real.
Move with the arrow keys or [W] [A] [S] [D] . After the game ends: Enter = new, [S] = setup.
The tunnels on the left and right warp you to the other side.
The four ghosts hunt with their original behaviors: Blinky chases directly, Pinky sets up ambushes, Inky uses a vector via Blinky, Clyde backs off up close.
Power pellets make ghosts blue and edible for a while - the chain gives 200/400/800/1600 points. Fruit appears as a bonus, an extra life comes at 10,000 points.
Difficulty normal/hard/extreme sets ghost speed and frightened time; every level gets faster.
- Eat a power pellet only when several ghosts are close - the chain is what counts.
- Remember the scatter phases: at every switch all ghosts turn around.
[Space], arrow up, [W] or a mouse click makes the bird flap - it tilts with its climb and sink speed.
Every pipe passed gives one point. Coins (bonus) and a shield power-up that forgives exactly one collision appear in the gaps.
Day and night themes change with the score; after the game over there are medals from bronze to platinum.
- Short, regular taps keep the flight path calmer than rare long ones.
- The difficulty sets gap size and speed - the gap narrows as your score grows.
The doodler jumps automatically on landing - you only steer left/right (with inertia). The edges are open: leaving left brings you back in on the right.
Shoot upwards with arrow up or [Space] .
- Green: normal. Blue: moves. Brown: breaks when stepped on. White: vanishes after one jump.
- Springs give a super jump, the propeller hat carries you up automatically for a moment (invulnerable).
- Monsters are deadly on contact - shooting them gives extra points.
Score = height reached; difficulty rises with height.
- Plan where to land before jumping off - brown platforms won't carry you.
- Use the open edge as a shortcut to far-away platforms.
Arrows or [W] [A] [S] [D] slide all tiles in one direction at once. Equal numbers merge into their sum; after every move a new tile appears.
The goal is the 2048 tile - after that it continues endlessly. You lose when no move is possible.
Every merge adds the value of the new tile to your score.
- Park your biggest tile in a corner and never disturb that corner.
- Slide mainly in two directions - it keeps the board sorted.
Left click reveals a cell, right click places a flag (optionally with a question-mark cycle, [Q] in the setup). [F] flags the cell under the cursor, [R] restarts.
Chording: clicking a satisfied number (all flags placed) reveals the remaining neighbors at once.
Beginner (9x9, 10 mines), intermediate (16x16, 40) and expert (30x16, 99). The best time per level is saved.
The first click is always safe - mines are placed only afterwards. Points = level base value minus seconds.
- Start with the numbers at the edge of open areas - the patterns there are unambiguous.
- A 1 in a corner with only one covered neighbor is always a safe flag.
Select a cell with the arrow keys, [W] [A] [S] [D] or a mouse click - the number pad on the right works entirely with the mouse.
- [1] to [9] enters a digit (numpad works too).
- [0], Backspace or right click erases.
- [N] toggles note mode, [H] gives a hint, [R] restarts the level, [Q] opens the level select.
- After the game ends, [A] hides the banner and reveals the full solution.
400 fixed levels: 4 difficulties (easy/normal/hard/expert) times 100 levels. Every level is the same puzzle everywhere and uniquely solvable; solved levels get ticked off.
The game mode sets the assists and the score multiplier:
- Classic x2.0: no assists, pure like on paper.
- Notes x1.5: plus pencil notes.
- Comfort x1.0: errors red instantly, conflict highlighting, correct entries lock in.
- Assist x0.7: additionally up to 3 hints.
Every entry is checked against the solution immediately. With the 3-error limit active (setup, key [F] ) the third mistake ends the game.
Points = (difficulty base minus time, errors and hints) times the mode multiplier.
- Start with rows, columns and boxes that already hold many digits.
- Note candidates in pairs: if two cells share the same two candidates, they drop out everywhere else.
- In classic mode take your time: every mistake counts immediately, even without a red mark.
Hop cell by cell with the arrow keys or [W] [A] [S] [D] .
- [R] restarts, [S] opens the setup.
After the game over: [Enter] = retry.
At the bottom 5 traffic lanes with cars and trucks in alternating directions - contact is deadly.
Above, 5 river lanes: logs and turtles carry you; falling into the water means drowning. Turtles dive periodically on higher levels (blinking = warning).
At the top wait 5 bays - filling all of them completes the level, then everything speeds up.
- Extras: a bonus fly (+200) appears briefly in empty bays, crocodiles occupy bays on higher levels (landing = death), and the time bar at the bottom drains per frog.
Every newly reached row gives 10 points, a bay 50 plus 10 per remaining second.
All 5 bays award 1000 points and the next level.
At 10,000 points you get a one-time extra life (start: 3 lives).
- Plan traffic gaps one lane ahead instead of waiting at the edge.
- Use logs drifting towards your target bay as a taxi.
- Land early: the time bonus beats a detour to the fly.
Flip cards with a mouse click - or move the frame with arrows/WASD and flip with [Space] or [Enter] .
- [R] shuffles a new round, [S] opens the setup.
A mismatched pair stays visible briefly and then flips back by itself.
Three board sizes: 4x4 (8 pairs), 6x6 (18) and 8x6 (24) - the motifs are shape-color combinations.
Solo, every revealed two-card combination counts as a move; the clock is running.
- Duel (multiplayer on the pre-game screen): take turns flipping, a match means you go again - whoever has more pairs at the end wins.
Solo: board-size base minus 15 per move and 2 per second (minimum 100).
Duel: the winner's pairs times 100 go to the high-score list.
- Flip unknown cards first - each one shows you a motif for free.
- Anchor motifs by their color group, it halves the search space.
- In a duel never reveal a fresh pair for your opponent.
Drag cards with the mouse (drag & drop) or move them click-by-click; right click sends the top card to the foundation (Klondike/FreeCell).
- [U] undoes any number of moves, [R] deals a new hand, [S] opens the setup.
[Space] or [Enter] operates the stock (draw/deal).
- Klondike: the classic solitaire - four foundations from ace to king, tableau descending in alternating colors; option: draw 1 or 3.
- Spider: 10 columns, 104 cards - complete king-to-ace runs of one suit vanish; option: 1, 2 or 4 suits.
- FreeCell: everything face up, 4 free cells; supermoves are limited by free cells and empty columns.
- Pyramid: remove pairs summing to 13, the king counts alone; 2 redeals.
- TriPeaks: always one rank above or below the waste pile (ace and king wrap) - long chains give combo points.
Klondike: +10 per foundation card, +5 per revealed card, time bonus on winning. FreeCell: +10 per foundation card plus time bonus.
Spider: 500 minus moves plus 100 per completed run. Pyramid: +5 per card, +500 for clearing.
TriPeaks: 10 times combo per card - the stock resets the combo; +500 for clearing.
Draw-3 (Klondike) and the Spider suit count are saved permanently.
Undo is unlimited and free - feel free to experiment.
All variants share one high-score list.
- Free aces and twos as early as possible (Klondike/FreeCell).
- Keep one column empty - it is your most important tool (Spider/FreeCell).
- In Pyramid, count the reachable 13-pairs before touching the stock.

The mouse steers the camera directly like in a shooter: every movement turns the view instantly by that amount (the cursor is captured invisibly inside the window). [Esc] pauses and releases the mouse. Yaw is unlimited, up/down clamps at 60 degrees.
Left click shoots exactly through the screen center (short cooldown between shots).
- [+] and [-] change the sensitivity (even mid-game), [E] ends a chill session.
- Precision (60 s): always 3 orbs at once - shooting one spawns a new one instantly; an accuracy bonus is added at the end.
- Reflex (30 targets): targets appear one at a time and shrink away after a moment - reaction time counts, stats at the end.
- Moving targets (60 s): orbs drift on paths (swinging, orbiting, bobbing) - consecutive hits raise the combo multiplier.
- Chill (endless): no timer, no miss penalty - just relax and shoot; the score is saved when you return to the menu.
Precision: 100 points per hit plus a distance bonus; at the end accuracy squared times 1500 on top.
Reflex: the faster the reaction, the more points (1000 minus milliseconds, at least 50).
Moving targets: 80 points times the combo multiplier (up to x4 at 12 consecutive hits) - a miss resets the combo.
Chill: 50 points times the multiplier; the combo only fades after 5 seconds without a hit.
- Space (default): a full star sphere, a black hole with a brightly glowing ring and a distant planet.
- Neon: a synthwave arena with a glowing floor grid and a striped sun.
- Range: an indoor hall with lanes, lamps and classic bullseye targets. Theme and adjustable motion blur (0 to 80 percent, key [B] or setup buttons) are saved.
- Small, calm mouse movements hit better than frantic swipes - the view follows 1:1.
- Low sensitivity for precision, higher for reflex and moving targets.
- Distant targets have a small forgiveness margin - hold steady instead of overcorrecting.
Two colours take turns dropping discs into one of 7 columns; each disc falls to the lowest free cell. The first to line up four - horizontally, vertically or diagonally - wins the round.
In single player you face the AI (three strengths in the setup); in 2-player mode you take turns at one mouse or keyboard.
The starting player alternates every round. [Enter] starts the next round, [S] returns to the setup.
- Mouse: hover over a column (the preview disc shows the spot) and click.
- Keyboard: [Left] [Right] pick the column, drop with [Down], [Space] or [Enter].
- Direct pick: the numbers [1] to [7] drop straight into that column.
Easy deliberately misses some threats and sometimes plays only the second-best move - great for learning. Medium plans a few moves ahead and blocks reliably.
Hard searches much deeper and punishes every mistake instantly - only double threats win here.
Every win against the AI scores one point; the highscore is the most wins in one session. There is no scoring in 2-player mode.
- The centre column is the strongest: most four-in-a-rows run through it.
- Build double threats (two open threes at once) - your opponent can only block one of them.
1-versus-1 in an arena of walls: hit your opponent to take the round - first to 5 rounds wins the match.
Shots bounce off walls once (ricochet) and vanish on the second contact. Careful: a bounced shot can hit you too.
Play against the AI (three strengths) or with two players on one keyboard. After the match: [Enter] = rematch, [S] = setup.
- Player 1: [W] [S] drive forward and back, [A] [D] turn, [Space] fires.
- Player 2: arrow keys drive and turn, [Enter] fires. The bindings follow the options.
- At most 4 of your shots live at once, with a short reload in between.
- Rapid fire: 8 seconds with almost no reload.
- Shield: absorbs exactly one hit (ring around the tank).
- Triple shot: the next 5 shots fan out in three directions. Power-ups appear every few seconds in the arena and expire after 12 seconds.
Four arenas to choose from: Open (no cover), Cross, Pillars and Maze - or Random, which rotates the arena every round.
The easy AI drives around aimlessly and aims poorly; the medium one chases you and sidesteps.
The hard AI keeps its distance, leads its shots ahead of your movement and even banks shots off walls on purpose.
Against the AI you score per match win: more for higher strengths and clean victories; points add up across rematches. There is no scoring in 2-player mode.
- Use the walls: banking shots around corners hits without exposing yourself.
Goal: get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Number cards count face value, pictures 10, the ace 11 or 1.
The game uses a 4-deck shoe; the dealer draws to 16 and stands on every 17.
Place your bet first (chip buttons or keys [1] to [4], [Backspace] clears it), then deal with [Enter].
- Hit [H]: draw another card.
- Stand [S]: keep your current total.
- Double [D]: double the bet, take exactly one card, then stand automatically - only on your first two cards.
- Split [X]: separate two equal-value cards into two hands (once per round; split aces get just one card each).
- Blackjack (ace + ten-value card) pays 3:2.
- A normal win pays 1:1, a push (tie) returns your bet.
- Bust or lose: the bet is gone. If the dealer shows an ace or a 10, they immediately check for blackjack.
You start with 500 chips; your balance and record are saved permanently and survive every restart.
The highscore is the highest chip balance you have ever reached.
Below 10 chips you are broke: [Enter] restarts with 500 fresh chips - the record stays.
- Basic strategy: against an upcard of 7 or higher draw to 17; against 4 to 6 stand early - the dealer often busts there.
- Always split aces and eights, never split tens.
You fly through a curving neon tube, dodging bars, blocks and ring gates - one hit and the run is over.
Golden coins float in the gaps; they score extra points and usually mark the safe line.
Ring gates have exactly one hole: thread through it instead of dodging.
- Endless: the speed keeps rising and the gaps get tighter - how far can you get? A crash ends the run and saves the highscore.
- Levels: 30 fixed tracks with a finish line, from relaxed to brutal. Completed levels get ticked off; session points add up.
- Keys (default): [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrows push the ship around the tube.
- Mouse: toggle in the setup with [C] - direct 1:1 steering, the cursor is captured and [Esc] releases it.
- [B] cycles motion blur in 10-percent steps (0 to 80, saved).
- In level mode: [R] retries after a crash, [S] opens the selection.
- Endless: 10 points per metre plus 50 per coin.
- Levels: 1000 for the finish, 50 per coin and a time bonus when you beat the par time.
The level-mode highscore is your best session total - playing several levels in a row pays off.
- Watch the rings far ahead: the tube telegraphs its curve early enough to countersteer.
- Stay near the centre when possible - every gap is reachable from there.
50 seed-generated mazes that grow with every level. Find the green pulsing exit - it always sits at the point farthest from the start.
Blue orbs float around the maze; every collected orb earns bonus points.
Completed levels get ticked off in the selection; [Enter] at the finish starts the next one right away.
- First person (3D): Wolfenstein-style view with mouselook - right in the middle instead of above.
- Top-down (2D): the classic map from above, with no mouse capture at all. Toggle in the setup with [V]; the choice is saved.
- First person: [W] [S] forward and back, [A] [D] strafe, the mouse turns your view - or turn with [Q] and [E] on the keyboard.
- [M] toggles the minimap, [Esc] pauses and releases the mouse.
- Top-down: [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrows walk in world directions.
- Reaching the exit: 500 points.
- Per orb: 100 extra points.
- Plus a time bonus when you beat the level's par time; session points add up to the highscore.
- Right-hand rule: always following the same wall is guaranteed to reach the exit.
- The orbs roughly line the way to the exit - collecting them usually means you are on track.

Reversi (Othello) is played on an 8x8 board. You place a disc so that one or more of the opponent's discs are trapped in a straight line between the new disc and another disc of your colour - horizontally, vertically or diagonally. All trapped discs flip to your colour.
A move is only legal if it flips at least one disc. If you have no legal move, your turn is passed automatically. When neither player can move, the game ends and whoever has more discs wins.
In single player you (Black) face the AI; in two-player mode Black and White alternate.
- Mouse: click an empty square. Legal squares are marked with a small dot.
- Keyboard: the arrow keys (or your movement keys) move the selection frame, [Space] or [Enter] places the disc.
- After a round: [Enter] = new round, [S] = back to setup (single player only).
Easy plays mostly at random, Medium looks a few moves ahead, Hard searches deeper and values the corners highly.
- Corners are golden: a disc in a corner can never be flipped again.
- Beware the squares next to a corner - they often hand the corner to your opponent.
- Having fewer discs but more mobility in the midgame is often better than having many.
Every win against the AI is worth one point; the high score is the most wins in a session. Two-player games are not scored.
You have 5 dice and up to 3 rolls per turn. After each roll you may keep any dice and reroll only the rest. Then you record the result in exactly one of the 13 categories.
Each category can be used only once. If nothing fits, you cross one out for 0 points. After 13 turns the sheet is full and the game is over.
Single player is a high-score chase for the highest total; in two-player mode you fill two sheets in turns - the higher total wins.
Upper section (Ones to Sixes): counts the pips of that number. If your upper section totals at least 63, you earn a 35-point bonus.
- Three/Four of a kind: sum of all dice if at least 3 resp. 4 are the same.
- Full house = 25 (three plus a pair), Small straight = 30 (four in a row), Large straight = 40 (five in a row), Yahtzee = 50 (five of a kind), Chance = sum of all dice (always allowed).
- [Space] or the Roll button rerolls the dice that are not held.
- Click a die or press [1] to [5] to hold or release that die.
- Click a category or pick it with the arrow keys and press [Enter] to score it.
- After the game: [Enter] restarts.
- Grab the 63-point upper bonus early - fives and sixes are especially valuable.
- Use Chance to rescue a bad roll; cross out Yahtzee or a straight if nothing works out.

Guess the hidden 5-letter word within 6 attempts. After each guess the tiles change colour: green = right letter in the right spot, yellow = the letter appears but somewhere else, grey = the letter is not in the word.
Repeated letters are handled correctly: a letter is only marked yellow or green as often as it actually occurs in the answer.
Every guess must be 5 letters, but need not be a 'real' word - it is not checked against a dictionary. The answers match the selected language.
- Type letters A-Z, [Backspace] deletes the last one, [Enter] checks the row (only with 5 letters).
- You can also use the on-screen keyboard with the mouse; its letters colour in based on what you have learned so far.
It goes on endlessly: each solved word scores points - fewer guesses means more (10 to 60). A new word appears right after.
The first word you FAIL to crack ends the game; the points you gathered are your high score.
- Open with a word that has many different, common letters.
- Use grey letters to rule things out and move yellow letters to a new position.
Start running with [Space] or [Up] - the dino then runs automatically.
- Jump: tap [Space]/[Up] for small hops, hold for higher jumps.
- Duck: hold [Down] - in the air this makes you fall faster.
Cacti appear singly or in groups on the ground - jump over them.
Pterodactyls show up at three heights: high = duck, low/mid = jump.
Speed keeps rising; every 100 points you get a beep and a short blink.
Toggle on the start screen (saved): [1]-[3] difficulty, [N] day/night, [C] skin.
- Tapping briefly saves height for quick double obstacles.
- After a crash, continue right away with [Enter]/[Space].
Chosen in setup - each with 1 player vs AI or 2 players local:
- German Draughts 8x8: men capture forwards and backwards, the king flies any distance.
- International Draughts 10x10: bigger board, forced capture with the maximum rule (longest capture is mandatory).
- Checkers 8x8 (English): men capture forwards only, the king moves just one square.
Captures are forced: if a capture exists you must take it - capturable pieces are outlined in red.
Click a piece, then the target square; play a multi-jump step by step.
Keyboard: [Arrows]/[WASD] move the frame, [Space]/[Enter] selects.
A man reaching the far row becomes a king (crown).
Single-player offers three AI strengths (minimax + alpha-beta), pick them in setup with [<]/[>].
The high score counts your wins against the AI this session; multiplayer is not scored.
After a game: [Enter] new round, [S] back to setup.
Pick the variant in the pre-game screen:
- Texas Hold'em: against 1-3 AI opponents, with dealer button, blinds and four betting rounds (preflop, flop, turn, river).
- 5 Card Draw: heads-up vs AI - swap cards once, two betting rounds.
- Video Poker (Jacks or Better): solo against the paytable.
During betting: [F] fold, [C] check/call, [R] raise, [A] all-in - or click the buttons.
When swapping/holding: click cards or press [1]-[5], then [Enter] to draw.
[Enter]/[Space] deals the next hand.
Chips (start 1000) persist (mem.json). The high score is your highest chip count. Broke = restart with a click.
Hand ranking: High Card < Pair < Two Pair < Three of a Kind < Straight < Flush < Full House < Four of a Kind < Straight Flush < Royal Flush.
Put the numbered tiles back in order (1, 2, 3 …); the gap stays in the bottom-right corner.
Tiles can only slide into the empty gap. Three sizes: 3×3 (easy), 4×4 (classic) and 5×5 (hard).
The board is shuffled with many random moves, so it is always solvable.
- Click a tile in the same row or column as the gap to slide the whole line.
- Arrow keys push the tile next to the gap into it.
You start with a base score per size; every move and every second subtract a little. Solving fast and with few moves gives the best high score.
After solving, Enter/click starts a fresh board right away.
The computer picks a hidden code of coloured pegs (colours may repeat). Crack it row by row.

After each guess you get feedback pegs: a BLACK peg = right colour in the right spot, a WHITE peg = right colour in the wrong spot. The order of the feedback pegs does not reveal which peg it refers to.
Modes: Easy (4 pegs, 6 colours, 12 rows), Classic (4/6, 10 rows) and Hard (5 pegs, 8 colours).
- Click a colour at the bottom (or keys 1–8) to fill the next empty slot.
- Click a placed peg to clear it; < or Backspace removes the last one.
- OK or Enter checks the full row.
Like Wordle it is an endless streak: each cracked code scores points (fewer guesses + harder mode = more), then a new code appears at once.
The first code you fail to crack ends the game - the total is your high score.
Shoot bubbles up into the honeycomb field. When three or more of the same colour touch, the group pops.
Bubbles that lose their link to the top row when a group pops fall down and give bonus points.
Modes: Easy (4 colours, no new rows), Classic (5 colours, an extra row drops in now and then) and Hard (6 colours, faster).
- The cannon aims at the mouse; left/right arrows also turn it.
- Left-click or Space shoots. Bubbles bounce off the side walls.
- The small bubble to the left of the cannon is your next colour.
Popped and dropped bubbles score points; clearing the whole field gives a bonus.
As soon as a bubble locks in below the red line the game is over - the total is your high score.
Guess the hidden word letter by letter. Each wrong letter draws another part of the hangman.
After 6 mistakes the figure is complete and the round is lost.
Modes by word length: Short words (3–5), Mixed (3–12) and Long words (7–12). Words match the selected language and use only A–Z.
- Type letters A–Z or click them on the on-screen keyboard.
- Correct letters appear in the word; wrong ones turn the key grey.
Endless streak: each guessed word scores points (more remaining lives and longer words = more), then a new word appears at once.
The first loss ends the game - the total is your high score.
A 3D Minecraft-style platformer: jump across floating block platforms to the glowing goal beacon. Every level is a fresh, seed-generated parkour and gets harder.
The camera is first-person like Minecraft by default; press V to switch to a chase camera.
Fall below the platforms and you lose a life and respawn at the last checkpoint. At 0 lives (you start with 3) the run ends.
Every block carries a real pixel texture: grass with its green overhang, dirt, stone, oak planks, the diamond block at the goal, slime blocks and wood for ladders and fences.

On top of that: the Steve figure with a walk cycle in the chase camera, the first-person hand, the beacon beam above the goal, spinning gold ingots as coins, a square sun, pixel clouds and hearts in the HUD.
Press T to change the texture detail: high, low or off. On slower machines 'low' or 'off' runs noticeably smoother; your choice is saved.
- WASD or arrow keys: move (relative to where you look). Space: jump. Mouse: look around.
- On a ladder, W climbs up and S climbs down. A spring block launches you high into the air.
- V = view (first/third person), B = motion blur, C = capture/release mouse, +/- = sensitivity. Esc pauses and frees the mouse.
- T = texture detail (high/low/off).
- Grass/dirt/stone/wood: solid blocks you jump on and stand on.
- Ladder: climb up/down slowly. Fence: a small block that blocks the path - just jump over it.
- Spring block: launches you high (to reach tall platforms). Coins float along the route for extra points.
Each coin is worth 50 points. Reaching a level's goal gives 1000 points plus a time bonus (the faster, the more).
Points accumulate across all levels; the total is your high score.
Enemies march along the path in waves. Build towers next to it to stop them before the exit - every breakthrough costs lives (bosses 5), at 0 the run ends.
Every map is endless: waves keep growing stronger and a boss arrives every 8 waves. Between waves you build at your leisure; you start the next one yourself.
Kills earn gold, plus wave bonuses and 5% interest. Locked maps unlock via your best wave.
- Click a tower card (or 1-9), then place it on the field. Right-click cancels.
- Click a tower: Upgrade [U] (up to 3 levels), Sell [X] (70% back). In Maximal mode you pick an A/B specialisation at top level.
- [Space] starts the wave, [F] = 2x speed, [G] = show all ranges, mouse wheel scrolls the build bar. Maximal: [Q] Meteor, [W] Frost Nova, [E] Gold Rush.
- Arrow = fast & cheap, Cannon = area damage, Frost = slows & reveals, Sniper = huge range, pierces armor, hits flyers.
- Classic adds Poison (damage over time), Tesla (chain lightning, anti-air) and Banner (+20% damage aura).
- Maximal only: Mortar (arcing shots across most of the field), Flak (anti-air), Laser (continuous beam with ramping damage) and Gold Bank (income per wave).
- Runts, sprinters, swarms and tanks form the base; armored, regenerating and splitting enemies join later.
- Maximal only: flyers take the direct air route (only Sniper/Tesla/Flak/Laser hit them), cloaked enemies are visible only near Frost, Banner or Sniper towers, healers patch up their neighbours.
- Every 8th wave a boss marches in: lots of health, 5 lives lost on breakthrough, big reward.
- Classic = the main mode with 7 towers. Compact = 4 towers, 2 levels, more starting gold - the quick start. Maximal = 11 towers, A/B branches, special enemies and active abilities.
- Meadow (free), Canyon (from wave 5), Crossroads (from 10, the path crosses itself - strong for towers, but enemies are tougher) and Gauntlet (from 15, you may only build right next to the path).
Points come from every kill plus a wave bonus that grows with wave number and map difficulty. The milestone sits at 10,000 points - roughly wave 18-20 on Meadow.

Minigolf across 360 holes: 18 hand-built and 342 generated. The Classic and Pro courses ease you in with nine built holes each, the Tour offers 38 courses of nine generated holes with rising difficulty, and Random draws nine holes from everything and mirrors them at random.

Tour holes come from a seed: course 7, hole 3 looks the same on every start - nothing has to be stored for that. The arrows beside the course number page through the 38 courses, with the total par next to them.
The goal is to sink the ball in as few strokes as possible. After eight strokes the ball is picked up and the hole is scored at the minimum.
In two-player mode each player takes the same hole one after the other; the scorecard on the right shows par and both results.
- Move the mouse to aim. Hold the left mouse button to load power, release to putt.
- Left/right arrows aim, up/down set the power, [Space] putts.
- [G] toggles the aim line - you can also switch it off for good in the setup screen.
- Sand slows the ball down hard, ramps accelerate in the direction of the arrows.
- Water costs a penalty stroke; the ball returns to its last safe spot.
- Rubber bumpers give speed back; windmills and moving blocks are all about timing.
Every hole is worth 600 points plus 300 for each stroke under par (and 300 less for each stroke over, never below 100).
A hole in one adds 500 points. The sum of all holes is your high score; the lowest stroke count per course is stored on top of that.

A pinball machine with three tables: Classic with three pop bumpers and one drop target bank, Space with four bumpers in a diamond and two banks, Lama with an open playfield and six targets in an arc.
Each game gives you 3 or 5 balls. After the launch a six second ball save runs: lose the ball in that window and it comes straight back to the shooter lane.
In two-player mode both players alternate ball by ball; the scores sit below each other in the info column.
- Hold the action key ([Space] by default) to load the plunger, release to launch. Pulled too softly? The ball rolls back and you may shoot again.
- Left/right (plus left/right [Shift]) work the flippers. With the mouse: left half of the screen = left flipper, right half = right flipper.
- The up key nudges the table. Three nudges in quick succession trigger TILT - the flippers stay dead until the ball drains.
Pop bumpers score 100, slingshots 50 and drop targets 250 - all times the current multiplier (up to x5).
Clearing a full target bank or collecting all four L-A-M-A lanes raises the multiplier by one.
Three balls locked in the saucer start multiball: three balls at once, and the bumpers pay a 2,500 point jackpot.
The info column on the right shows the multiplier, locked balls, cleared banks and the remaining ball save time.
A nudge saves a ball that is about to drain - but use it sparingly: the counter only resets after four quiet seconds.
The best result is stored per table, and the score of a game counts as your high score.
Ten frames by the official rules: two rolls per frame, strikes and spares earn bonus points, and the tenth frame grants bonus balls. The maximum is a 300 game.
The scorecard right below the header shows all ten frames with their rolls (X, /, -) and the running total.
In two-player mode both players alternate frame by frame.
1. Position on the foul line, 2. aiming angle, 3. spin (hook left or right), 4. power.
Every slider swings on its own; the action key or a click locks it in.
Left/right let you set a slider by hand instead - the swinging stops as soon as you do.
The lane is oiled up front: the hook only bites in the last third and then pulls the ball into the pocket between pins 1 and 3.
Leave the lane sideways and the ball drops into the gutter - that roll counts zero.
On Pro the sliders swing faster and the lane scatters a little more; on Easy everything is calmer. [G] toggles the guide line.
The ten pins are circles with real mass: the ball hits them, they knock each other over. A strike is the result of physics, not of luck.
The game total is your high score; the best result per difficulty is stored as well.
